summary: All six round-1 findings are fixed. Current DNS proof now reclaims a hostname from a stale binding, re-verifying no longer interrupts an active route, and the new tests cover reserved hostnames and the `go` exception, the CLI and workspace forwarding, retrying domain cleanup on app removal, and the 429 rate limit. Three small items remain. The durable CLI test imports halo-cli by a relative path, so Turbo will not rerun it when the CLI changes. A temp DNS test does not tell the two DNS failure kinds apart. One type-only export line is uncovered and has no exemption.

findings.body: The durable test "runs domain commands through the workspace API" imports the CLI with `../../../packages/halo-cli/src/app.js`. `@get-halo/control-plane` does not depend on `@get-halo/cli`. CI runs `turbo run ... test:unit --affected`, and Turbo builds both its affected set and its cache hash from the package graph. A later change to `packages/halo-cli/src/app.ts` therefore will not rerun or invalidate this test, so the CLI behavior it is meant to guard goes unchecked. Fix: add `@get-halo/cli` as a devDependency of the control plane and import it through the package specifier, or export the command from the package. Otherwise, make the CLI part of this test a temp test and keep only the workspace-forwarding assertions as durable.

The loop over `ENODATA`, `ENOTFOUND` and `ETIMEOUT` only checks `toBeInstanceOf(Error)`. The behavior under test (AppDomains.ts:29-36) is that missing records become an empty answer. That gives an `AppDomainRequestError`, which the user sees as BAD_REQUEST. Real resolver failures become an `AppDomainHostError`, which the user sees as a 500. The current assertion passes even if the two are swapped. Assert `name: "AppDomainRequestError"` for ENODATA and ENOTFOUND, and `name: "AppDomainHostError"` for ETIMEOUT.

testRequests.rationale: This is a type-only re-export (`export type { AppDomain, AppDomainDnsRecord }`) that is erased at compile time. Add a coverage-exempt comment saying so. Do not add a test.
